mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, increasing present value and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism operates in any monetary regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0%, it indicates a tight labor market that increases corporate profitability through higher wage growth and reduced labor turnover, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where both HOUST and RSAFS rise, or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05 in regression).

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening supply chain capacity and potential inflationary pressures, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors price in recession risk.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods with declining INDPRO, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption (measured by RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending that supports corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in any economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where RSAFS rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a rapidly strengthening labor market that boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE declines and PAYEMS rises, or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05 in regression).

mechanism_narrative: In post-shock recovery phases, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) relative to its 6-month moving average indicates persistent supply chain disruptions, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate prolonged inflation.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of post-shock recovery periods with declining INDPRO, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
